artDirection.style: academic studio-quality cannabis cultivation education; realistic botanical forms; cream/neutral background; natural green/flower colors; crisp vector labels layered over realistic or scientifically styled botanical imagery; no yellow cast; no decorative clutter
artDirection.textPolicy: Use short labels and callouts only. No paragraph blocks baked into artwork.
artDirection.colorPolicy: Do not rely on color alone; every maturity state and comparison must also have a text label or shape cue.
artDirection.copyrightPolicy: Create original artwork. Source papers constrain claims only; do not copy article figures, microscopy panels, or photographs.

briefs.queueTitle: Harvest Readiness: Multiple Signals, Not One
briefs.primaryMessage: Harvest readiness is a multi-signal assessment. Visual cues can narrow the harvest window, but genotype and crop context matter and no single cue is a universal trigger.
layout: Top title band: HARVEST READINESS — MULTIPLE SIGNALS, NOT ONE
Central realistic flowering cannabis inflorescence as the anchor image
Five surrounding evidence panels: stigma/pistil change, bract/flower development, glandular trichomes, overall plant/crop context, known genotype timing/history
Bottom decision strip: Observe → Compare → Sample consistently → Decide within genotype/context
requiredCallouts: Different genotypes can peak at different visual stages
Sample the same flower region under consistent lighting/magnification
forbiddenClaims: Do not state a universal percentage of amber pistils or trichomes as the correct harvest point
Do not claim amber trichomes directly equal a specific psychoactive effect
Do not imply plant fade or yellowing alone proves maturity
Do not present a fixed week number as universal
briefs.altText: Educational harvest-readiness diagram centered on a mature cannabis flower, comparing stigma color, flower development, trichome appearance, whole-plant context, and genotype-specific history as multiple signals rather than one universal harvest trigger.
briefs.caption: Harvest readiness is best treated as a multi-signal assessment. Stigma and trichome appearance can help define a harvest window, but genotype and crop context can shift when cannabinoid profiles peak.

scientific: All five signal panels are framed as observations, not guarantees
No universal amber percentage or week number
visual: Labels remain legible at mobile preview size

briefs.primaryMessage: Clear, cloudy/milky, and amber/brown glandular heads are observable maturation states, but trichomes on the same bract can mature asynchronously and their meaning is context-dependent.
layout: Top title band: TRICHOME MATURITY UNDER MAGNIFICATION
Three large matched-magnification botanical macro panels: CLEAR / CLOUDY-MILKY / AMBER-BROWN
Small anatomy key identifying stalk and glandular head
Asynchronous-maturation inset showing mixed clear, cloudy and amber heads on one bract
Bottom imaging-quality strip: same magnification + neutral white balance + same sample region
requiredLabels: Mixed maturity can occur on the same bract
requiredCallouts: Color is one observation, not a complete harvest decision
Genotype and plant age influence trichome development
forbiddenClaims: Do not label clear/cloudy/amber as exact THC percentages
Do not equate amber percentage with sedative versus energetic effects
Do not imply every trichome passes through states synchronously
Do not copy published microscopy images
briefs.altText: Matched-magnification educational comparison of clear, cloudy or milky, and amber or brown cannabis glandular trichomes, with an inset showing mixed maturity on one bract and a reminder to use consistent lighting and magnification.
briefs.caption: Cannabis glandular trichomes visibly change during maturation, but development is asynchronous and varies with genotype and plant age. Use trichome appearance as one observation within a broader harvest assessment.

scientific: Three maturity appearances match the evidence-supported sequence
No effect claims or THC-percentage claims
visual: All three panels use identical apparent magnification
Glandular heads remain distinct at mobile preview size
